Performance Benchmarks

Source: vignettes/articles/performance.Rmd
performance.Rmd

Spatial Markov workflows often run on tract panels with thousands of units and many periods. This article times griddy on a panel of that size and compares it with estdaR. It runs when the site is built, not during package checks.

library(griddy)
library(microbenchmark)
library(sf)
library(sfdep)
library(spdep)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

Synthetic grid panel

A 60 by 60 queen-contiguity grid over ten periods, 3,600 units in all, exercises the same classification and spatial-lag code as a tract-scale panel.

make_panel <- function(nx = 60, ny = 60, years = 2010:2019) {
  cells <- st_make_grid(st_bbox(c(xmin = 0, ymin = 0, xmax = nx, ymax = ny)), n = c(nx, ny))
  grid <- st_sf(id = seq_along(cells), geometry = cells)

  panel <- tidyr::crossing(id = grid$id, year = years) |>
    left_join(st_drop_geometry(grid), by = "id") |>
    mutate(value = id + as.integer(factor(year)) + rnorm(n())) |>
    left_join(select(grid, id, geometry), by = "id") |>
    st_as_sf()

  list(grid = grid, panel = panel)
}

fx <- make_panel()

geom <- fx$grid |>
  mutate(
    nb = st_contiguity(geometry),
    wt = st_weights(nb)
  )

listw <- nb2listw(geom$nb, glist = geom$wt, style = "W")

microbenchmark(
  classify = classify_dynamics(fx$panel, id, year, value, k = 5),
  markov = {
    cls <- classify_dynamics(fx$panel, id, year, value, k = 5)
    markov_dynamics(cls, id, year, class)
  },
  spatial = spatial_markov(fx$panel, id, year, value, geometry = geom, k = 5),
  times = 5
)
## Unit: milliseconds
##      expr      min       lq     mean   median       uq      max neval cld
##  classify 15.22166 15.29501 15.69858 15.39341 15.95019 16.63263     5 a  
##    markov 25.17289 27.02970 27.64828 27.64224 28.78905 29.60749     5  b 
##   spatial 39.54594 40.03355 41.70417 40.62407 42.54074 45.77654     5   c

Comparison against estdaR

The next chunk runs only when estdaR is installed. It calls griddy::spatial_markov() and estdaR::sp.mkv() on the same panel, with matched class breaks and identical weights, so any difference is implementation overhead.

wide_panel <- fx$panel |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = id, names_from = year, values_from = value) |>
  arrange(id)

wide_mat <- as.matrix(wide_panel |> select(-id))

bench <- microbenchmark(
  griddy = spatial_markov(fx$panel, id, year, value, geometry = geom, k = 5),
  estdaR = estdaR::sp.mkv(wide_mat, listw, classes = 5, fixed = TRUE),
  times = 5
)
bench
## Unit: milliseconds
##    expr      min       lq     mean   median       uq      max neval cld
##  griddy 37.31176 39.98796 39.62876 39.99423 40.27774 40.57212     5  a 
##  estdaR 27.82916 29.20024 30.71335 30.89699 31.02741 34.61298     5   b
# griddy's median time as a multiple of estdaR's
medians <- summary(bench)$median
round(medians[1] / medians[2], 1)
## [1] 1.3

griddy is somewhat slower, and the gap is bookkeeping. estdaR::sp.mkv() works directly on a unit-by-period matrix. griddy reshapes a long panel, classifies it, and keeps unit, time, class, and spatial-lag labels attached to every transition. Transition counts and spatial lags are computed in single vectorized passes, with no per-unit or per-period grouping.
